## ⭐ This card is now HALF answered by a merge — and the surviving half is sharper than the original question

`domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`. ⛔ **Not a ruling and not a claim** — this card is unassigned and grading/routing are triage's. This is a measurement that changes what the card is asking.

**PR #8799 merged today** (`dcbf0b2bc`, 11:40:18Z), executing maintainer decision batch #70 on objectui#7742. One of its four rows **declares `navigation`** — i.e. it took this card's first option, without this card being the vehicle. Its docblock says so in as many words:

> `navigation` is DECLARED on `KanbanSchema` since objectui#7742 (gantt precedent objectui#5903)

## Re-measured on `origin/main` `dcbf0b2bc` by this seat

Per-interface, by locating each `export interface` block and scanning only its own body — ⛔ not a file-level grep, which would have credited one interface with another's declaration:

| interface | file | `navigation` declared? |
|---|---|---|
| `ObjectGridSchema` | `objectql.ts` lines 641–1038 | ✅ **:963** |
| `ObjectViewSchema` | `objectql.ts` lines 1808–1992 | ✅ **:1856** |
| `KanbanSchema` | `complex.ts` | ✅ **:347** ← **new, from PR #8799** |
| **`ObjectKanbanSchema`** | `objectql.ts` lines **2816–2966** | ⛔ **NONE** |

**Firing control:** two of the four interfaces return a line number on the same instrument, so the `NONE` is a reading and not a matcher that scans nothing.

And the read site is now cast-free — `packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx:908`:

```ts
const navConfig = schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' };
```

⚠️ This card recorded it at `:822` as `(schema as any).navigation`; both the line and the spelling have moved.

## ⇒ What the card is actually asking now

`ObjectKanban`'s schema prop is the union `ObjectKanbanSchema | KanbanSchema`. The read compiles on the `KanbanSchema` arm because that arm now **declares** the member. On the `ObjectKanbanSchema` arm it still compiles **only through `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any`** — admitted, never examined.

So the original finding — *"read off the kanban node and declared on neither arm"* — is now:

> **Declared on the `kanban` arm and still undeclared on the `object-kanban` arm.** One renderer, two node types, and a `type: "object-kanban"` document's `navigation` is accepted with any value while a `type: "kanban"` one is judged.

That is **narrower and more concrete** than the question this card was filed with, and it is worth ruling as such rather than as the original. ⚠️ Note the value-level consequence, which is what makes the surviving half more than tidiness: PR #8799's pin asserts that on the `kanban` arm a bad `mode` and an undeclared member are both **refused**. On `object-kanban` neither is — `navigation: { mode: 'not-a-mode' }` passes.

## ⭐ And it is the THIRD instance of one pattern, which is the part worth ruling once

Batch #70 reached the `kanban` arm and stopped there. Three keys are now split across the two arms of the same renderer:

| key | `kanban` arm | `object-kanban` arm | card |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowCollapse` | retired (`?: never` + named refusal) | still declared and still zero-read | objectui#8801 |
| `titleField` | retired on this arm | declared and kept (objectui#7322 item ②) | objectui#8802 (registry `inputs` divergence) |
| **`navigation`** | **declared and judged** | **undeclared, rides the index signature** | **this card** |

⇒ Whoever rules any of the three should know the other two exist. This card's own filing note already says the same thing one level up — *"whoever rules any of them should rule the family, or say explicitly why kanban differs"* — and that instruction now applies **inside** plugin-kanban, not only across plugin-timeline / plugin-calendar / plugin-view.

## ⛔ What is NOT claimed

- ⛔ Not claimed the card should close. Its own subject survives on one arm, and its cross-package siblings (objectui#8654 plugin-timeline, objectui#8651 plugin-calendar) are untouched by this merge — I did **not** re-measure those two, and the rows above assert nothing about them.
- ⛔ Not claimed batch #70 intended to answer this card. It ruled objectui#7742, which reached the same key from the enforce-or-remove direction. Two cards converging on one key is exactly the reconciliation this comment exists to make visible.
- ⛔ No label, priority or `domain:*` touched.

Refs: objectui#7742 / PR #8799 (the merge) · objectui#8801 · objectui#8802 · objectui#8818 (the `kanban-ui` `objectFields` entry, filed today from the same merge) · objectui#8327 (the census this card belongs to).

**Triage — objectui#8327 family (8 cards). `domain:spec` · `pm:queue`. ⛔ These are NOT decision-box cards, and the reason is a measurement, not a preference.**

Taken **2026-09-10T13:39Z** (clock read in the same call that posts this).

### The ruling that governs all eight

Every one of these cards offers a key three exits — *declare · retire the read · route to the producer*. ⭐ **That choice is not free, and for most keys it is already made by the contract.**

`packages/types` in this repo is a **mirror**, not an authority: `objectql.ts` re-exports from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`KanbanConfig`, `ListColumn`, `SelectionConfig`, `PaginationConfig`, …) and its own docblocks say so — *"Aligned with @objectstack/spec ListViewSchema.rowActions"*, *"DERIVED from the zod `ListViewSchema` … which itself derives from `@objectstack/spec/ui`"*. ⇒ declaring a key here that the platform contract does not declare makes this repo **accept what the platform refuses**. SKILL.md settles that direction outright:

> 协议为基准:spec 与代码不一致默认改代码对齐;改协议单独立卡,⛔ 不作缺陷卡的选项。

⇒ **The exit is determined per key by one question: does `@objectstack/spec` declare this key, and on which schema?**

- **declared in spec** ⇒ align the mirror. That is *restoring declared = enforced*, a named non-escalating class. Mechanical.
- **not declared in spec** ⇒ ⛔ "declare" is **off the table** on this card. The exit is retire-the-read or route-to-producer. Also mechanical.

Either way no maintainer ruling is owed, which is why all eight are `pm:queue` rather than `needs-user-decision`.

### The screening measurement — with both controls

Word-frequency over `packages/spec/src/ui/` on objectstack `origin/main`:

| key | hits | key | hits |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| `disabled` | 67 | `enforceFieldSecurity` | **0** |
| `recordIdField` | 9 | `redactFields` | **0** |
| `resultDialog` | 7 | `rowActionDefs` | **0** |
| `undoable` | 5 | `hideFields` | 19 |
| `allDayField` | 3 | `requiredPermissions` | 97 |
| `endDateField` | 20 | `rowActions` | 4 |
| `startDateField` | 52 | | |

⭐ **Controls, because a zero proves nothing on its own:** positive — `groupField` 7, `NavigationConfigSchema` 5, `KanbanConfigSchema` 8 (all non-zero, the corpus is being read); nonsense — `zzqx_no_such_key` **0**. ⇒ the three zeros above are readings.

⚠️ **What this screening does and does not establish.** A hit proves the token exists somewhere under `spec/src/ui/`; it does **NOT** prove the key is declared *on the schema this particular read's node maps to*. ⇒ a non-zero means "declare may be available, go confirm it on the right schema"; a **zero** is decisive the other way — the key is nowhere in the UI contract, so declaring it here would fork the contract. **Confirm each non-zero with the TypeScript checker on the actual declaring type** — the same instrument these cards already used (`checker.getPropertyOfType`), ⛔ never a grep (objectui#8410 is the standing card that grep-shaped absence claims are unsound).

---

### ⭐ `navigation` — measured, and the answer is the opposite of the obvious one

Three cards read `navigation` off a **node** (#8652 kanban, #8654 timeline, #8651's `CalendarSchema` arm) while the grid/view faces declare it. The tempting fix is "declare it on the other arms too, for consistency". **Measured on objectstack `origin/main`, `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`:**

```
1929   /** Navigation / Interaction */
1930   navigation: NavigationConfigSchema.optional().describe('Configuration for item click navigation (page, drawer, modal, etc.)'),
...
1936   kanban: KanbanConfigSchema.optional().describe('Kanban-board configuration — applies when the view renders as a kanban layout'),
```

⇒ in the platform contract `navigation` is a property **of the view**, and `kanban` is a *type-specific config block sitting beside it under that same view*. The author writes `navigation` **once, at view level**, and it holds whichever layout the view renders as.

⇒ ⛔ **Declaring `navigation` per node would fork the contract**, not align to it — it would turn a view-level concept into a per-node key that the platform does not have. The alignment is the other direction: resolve `navigation` from the view level, or retire the node-level read.

⚠️ **This ruling is hung on one named, falsifiable premise, and the dev must test it before the first edit:**

> **P1 — every kanban / timeline / calendar node that reads `navigation` is rendered inside a view that can carry it.**

Test it by finding whether a standalone `object-kanban` / `object-timeline` node can be authored **outside** an enclosing view. ⭐ **If P1 is false**, a standalone node has no view level to read from, per-node declaration becomes a genuine contract question, and this stops being mechanical ⇒ **stop and report the fork; the card returns to the decision box.** ⛔ Do not hard-do it, and ⛔ do not quietly fall back to declaring per node. A clean stop on a falsified premise is a full success here.

## This card carries the `navigation` family

⇒ **objectui#8652 is the family carrier.** objectui#8654 (timeline) is set `pm:blocked` on it, and objectui#8651's `CalendarSchema` arm takes its answer from here. Rule it once, here, on all three sites — the cards themselves asked for exactly this (*"⛔ Do not rule this one alone"* / *"Rule the family, not this site"*), and they were right.

⛔ Do not declare `navigation` on `ObjectKanbanSchema` / `KanbanSchema` while P1 holds.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — one concept, three sites, plus the P1 probe which is the real gate.
